counterexamples: S(x+y) and S(x)+S(y) are distinct irreducibles of the N-through-Add-only system and evaluate equally
notes: N(x+y)→N(x)+N(y) alone has joining N-overlaps and a unique syntactic NF on the size≤5 unary-plus-one-Add census. Semantic canonicity still fails because S does not distribute. Installing S-distributivity then breaks local confluence (add_s_push_lc).
statement: Irreducibles of the unary tree TRS plus only N(x+y)→N(x)+N(y) are unique representatives of integer functions.
title: N-through-Add alone is a semantic canonical form
